rubrics.justification: Accurately identifies an expanded blastocyst with thinned zona and notes a compact ICM-like area and generally cohesive TE, while appropriately acknowledging limits of a single static image. Slight overconfidence in calling TE/ICM as top-tier from this frame prevents a perfect score.
Comprehensively integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, male factor context, endometrial thickness, prior IVF outcomes, and lifestyle with embryo quality and prognosis.

The reasoning is logical and internally consistent: strong morphology and favorable age/endometrium improve prognosis, while untested status and BMI temper expectations. Probability estimates are well supported.

Recommendations are well aligned with standard IVF practice: elective single embryo transfer for a good-quality Day 5 blastocyst in a 33-year-old, continuation of luteal support, avoidance of routine unsupported add-ons, and selective consideration of further workup after repeated failures.

Provides clear practical recommendations for current transfer and contingency planning for future cycles, including SET, luteal support, and selective uterine/male-factor reassessment. Slightly general in some areas, so not maximally specific.
